Ligand believes the adjusted total revenues and income is a more meaningful indicator of its business performance than the GAAP total revenues and income. Liquidity and Capital Resources As of September 30, 2026, Ligand had cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $447.4 million, compared with $733.5 million at December 31, 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by cash used for the XOMA acquisition, partially offset by the proceeds from the Company’s issuance of its convertible senior notes due 2031. As of September 30, 2026, including its equity investments and availability under its credit facility, Ligand has approximately $750 million of deployable capital available to pursue additional royalty acquisitions and strategic investments. 2026 Financial Guidance Ligand is raising its 2026 full year adjusted earnings per diluted share guidance and reaffirming its 2026 revenue guidance. Ligand now expects the following: • Royalty revenue of $225 million to $250 million (unchanged) • Captisol sales of $35 million to $40 million (unchanged) • Contract revenue of $10 million to $20 million (unchanged) • Total revenue of $270 million to $310 million (unchanged) • Adjusted earnings per diluted share 2 of approximately $9.50 to $9.75, raised from approximately $9.00 to $9.50 Third Quarter Corporate Highlights On July 14, 2026, Ligand completed the acquisition of XOMA Royalty, a biotechnology royalty aggregator. The acquisition strengthens Ligand’s royalty portfolio by adding seven commercial products, including Roche’s VABYSMO® (faricimab-svoa), Servier and Ipsen’s OJEMDA™ (tovorafenib), and Zevra Therapeutics’ MIPLYFFA® (arimoclomol). Additionally, the acquisition adds 14 late-stage development programs, featuring Takeda’s mezagitamab and certain assets from Takeda’s externalized asset portfolio, including osavampator, volixibat, and OHB-607, along with more than 100 additional assets in various stages of development to Ligand’s portfolio. As a result, Ligand’s portfolio has more than doubled in size, now comprising over 200 commercial, clinical, and preclinical stage royalty assets. As a result, Ligand’s portfolio has more than doubled in size, now comprising over 200 commercial, clinical, and preclinical stage royalty assets. On September 22, 2026, Ligand announced the acquisition of a milestone and royalty interest in Santen Pharmaceutical’s Ryjunea from Sydnexis for a $23 million upfront payment. Under the terms of the agreement, Ligand acquired a 100% interest in certain payments and related rights under Sydnexis’s existing license agreement with Santen. The acquired payment rights include a tiered low-double-digit to high-teens royalty on Ryjunea net sales in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, as well as certain milestone payments. On September 24, 2026, Ligand announced it entered into a financing agreement with AvenCell Therapeutics, Inc., a clinical-stage cell therapy company developing controllable, allogeneic CAR-T therapies for patients with cancer, for up to $47 million. The investment is expected to help advance AvenCell’s pipeline, including AVC-201 for the treatment of relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and AVC-203 for the treatment of B-cell malignancies. Under the terms of the agreement, Ligand has committed up to $41 million in exchange for a mid single-digit to low double-digit royalty on worldwide annual net sales of all current and future AvenCell pipeline assets, with the applicable rate determined based on the total amount ultimately funded. The capital will be funded in four tranches, with the first tranche payable at closing, and the remaining three tranches payable upon achievement of certain predetermined clinical milestones and other specified financing conditions. Ligand has also committed up to $6 million in AvenCell’s concomitant Series C financing. 2 A reconciliation of forward-looking non-GAAP adjusted earnings per diluted share to the most directly comparable GAAP measure is not available without unreasonable effort, as certain items cannot be reasonably predicted because of their high variability, complexity and low visibility.
